title: Environment symbols (.NAME): lookup order and the cache
summary: An environment symbol is looked up as the interpreter does: the package's classes (CLASSES, PUBLICCLASSES, IMPORTEDCLASSES, then the REXX package's PUBLICCLASSES), then the package LOCAL, .local and .environment, asking the security manager (LOCAL / ENVIRONMENT) when there is one. rx::envValue keeps a found value while the epoch has not moved, and only while the three directories are plain: no SETMETHOD method table and no UNKNOWN method (Tom Dyer: 'it's only used in directory'). Those two Directory fields are found once at library load by calibration (directoryFields: a scratch Directory is given each feature in turn and the object words that change are recorded), never by sending a message. The specials .RS .LINE .CONTEXT .METHODS .RESOURCES .ROUTINES ask the manager first; an entry of that name wins; then the special value (RX_ENV_SPECIAL).
invariants: Never test a Directory by sending it INDEX, HASINDEX or HASMETHOD: they run the entry's method (a fixture printed '2 4 6 8' when this was tried).

Fixed classes (the package's classes, its imports, the REXX package's public classes) are found in copies of CLASSES / PUBLICCLASSES / IMPORTEDCLASSES taken once at library load (takeFixedClassTables) and read with StringTableAt: a lookup allocates nothing, as interpreted.
If calibration fails, the fallback (FINDCLASS) cannot tell an entry set to .nil from a missing one; it is correct otherwise.

provenance.claim: Environment cache, calibration, fixed class tables taken at load.
FixedClassTables: copies taken once, read with StringTableAt.
